ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ intersects the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{m}{x}$ where $x>0$, at points $A(1, 4)$ and $B(4, n)$. What are the expressions for the linear function and the inverse proportion function?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Substituting point A into the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{m}{x}\left(x>0\right)$, we have $m=xy=4$. Therefore, the expression of the inverse proportion function is: $y=\frac{4}{x}$. Hence, $4n=4$, solving this equation, we find $n=1$. Therefore, point $B(4, 1)$ is determined. This leads to the system $\left\{\begin{array}{l}1=4k+b\\ 4=k+b\end{array}\right.$, from which we solve $\left\{\begin{array}{l}k=-1\\ b=5\end{array}\right.$. Therefore, the equation of the linear function is: \boxed{y=-x+5};

This leads to the system $\left\{\begin{array}{l}1=4k+b\\4=k+b\end{array}\right.$, from which we solve $\left\{\begin{array}{l}k=-1\\b=5\end{array}\right.$. Therefore, the linear function is $y=-x+5$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are coordinate axes; in the first quadrant, a straight line slanting downward to the right is drawn, as well as an inverse proportional function curve in the first quadrant that gradually descends and approaches the coordinate axes; the two graphs intersect at the labeled points A and B. Then reason: The problem gives A=(1,4), B=(4,n), the straight line is y=kx+b, the inverse proportional function is y=m/x, and x>0. Because A is on the graph of the inverse proportional function, 4=m/1, so m=4; therefore the inverse proportional function is y=4/x. Because B=(4,n) is also on the graph of this inverse proportional function, n=4/4=1, that is, B=(4,1). The straight line passes through A(1,4) and B(4,1), and the slope k=(1-4)/(4-1)=-3/3=-1. Substitute A(1,4) into y=-x+b, obtaining 4=-1+b, so b=5. Therefore the linear function is y=-x+5, and the inverse proportional function is y=4/x.
